correctness.rationale: The proof reduces every possible three-coloring to the disjoint shore-palette patterns (1,1), (2,1), or (1,2). Because each edge then has a unique available color, the forest requirement becomes an exact acyclicity test for one or two complete bipartite edge-color classes. This forces the smaller shore to have size at most two. Explicit constructions attain three colors for shore sizes one and two, and a four-color star decomposition attains four for every K_{3,n}; the three-color obstruction supplies the matching lower bound. The finite verifier independently agrees on all K_{m,n} with 1<=m<=n<=6 and checks the K_{3,n} construction for 3<=n<=100; the infinite claim does not rely on this enumeration.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a complete infinite classification of three-colorability for the canonical complete-bipartite family and an exact infinite sharp-four family K_{3,n}. It sharpens the newly proved planar four-color theorem on every biclique with smaller shore at most two and identifies the first nonplanar shore size as a uniform four-color boundary. The palette-forcing proof is structural and reusable, rather than a finite lookup or routine one-parameter increment.
